title: CI blocked at scheduling by GitHub billing: fix in account Settings → Billing & plans
description: All 5 CI runs (including run 1 on the bootstrap commit) fail in ~3s with no runner and no steps. Signature of the repository Actions policy rejecting third-party actions (dtolnay/rust-toolchain, Swatinem/rust-cache, j178/prek-action). Fix: actions/checkout + actions/cache only; install toolchain via rustup from rust-toolchain.toml; install prek with pipx. If runs still fail identically after this, the cause is account-level (Actions disabled or billing) and must be fixed in repository settings.
acceptance_criteria: CI green on a PR and on main after merge.
notes: PR #3 merged 19:08 UTC. CI on main (run 35531330991) still refused at scheduling with the billing annotation; nothing further to do in the repository. Left open for the account owner: fix Billing & plans, then Actions → CI → Re-run jobs on main. First real CI run may surface runner issues (pipx install prek, cache paths); handle then.

title: Live incident.io: whoami and confirm API key scopes
description: cargo run -- incidentio whoami. Key must allow: view alerts, view incidents, manage alert tags, manage incident alerts. Record roles output in notes.
acceptance_criteria: Roles listed; missing scopes raised as issues.

title: Verify integration against real TypeSafe and incident.io accounts
description: Everything so far is asserted against documented examples and OpenAPI, never a live call. Run each path against real accounts and fix drift. Acceptance: every task below closed with observed responses noted.

title: Live TypeSafe call: triage all examples/alerts, record model id and distributions
description: cargo run -- triage examples/alerts/*.json --json with TYPESAFE_API_KEY. Note the versioned model in the response. Compare distributions to the expectations in policy tests; record surprises as follow-up issues.
acceptance_criteria: Three example alerts produce decisions; model id recorded in notes; no Decode errors.

title: Evaluate and tune triage quality on real alert history
description: Policy thresholds are conservative defaults from the TypeSafe docs, untuned. Build an evaluation loop before trusting automatic paging.

title: Evaluation harness: replay historical alerts and score decisions
description: Add signalman eval <dir>: run triage over a directory of alert JSON files with a labels.json (expected team, impact, action), output a confusion table per dimension and the distribution of confidences. Pin the model version in the run metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Report over at least 50 labelled alerts committed under evals/ (redacted).

title: OpenTelemetry tracing and metrics for the triage flow
description: Spans: webhook received, incident.io fetches, TypeSafe evaluate, write-back. Metrics: triage_total by decision and team, triage_duration_seconds, typesafe_input_tokens_total, upstream_errors_total by service and status. Export OTLP via tracing-opentelemetry + opentelemetry-otlp; keep fmt logging as fallback.
acceptance_criteria: OTLP export configurable via OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT; metrics visible in a local collector.

title: Production-harden the webhook receiver
description: signalman serve is functionally complete but has no request limits, no bounded concurrency for background triage, no metrics, and no container image.

title: Bound background triage concurrency and add per-request timeout
description: Background tokio::spawn per webhook is unbounded. Add a Semaphore (configurable, default 8) around Triager::triage_alert_by_id and a tokio::time::timeout (default 60s). Add tower-http body limit (64 KiB) and request timeout on the router.
acceptance_criteria: Load test with 200 concurrent deliveries shows bounded in-flight triages; tests cover the limit.

title: Live webhook end-to-end via Svix Play or ngrok
description: Expose signalman serve, add the endpoint in incident.io Settings → Webhooks subscribed to public_alert.alert_created_v1, send a test event, then fire a real alert. Verify signature passes, tags appear on the alert, and a confident duplicate attaches to the incident.
acceptance_criteria: One real alert triaged end to end with tags visible in incident.io.

title: Confirm multi-value status_category[one_of] filter on GET /v2/incidents
description: Client sends status_category[one_of]=triage&status_category[one_of]=live&status_category[one_of]=paused as repeated keys. Docs only show single values. Verify with cargo run -- incidentio open-incidents against a real account; if rejected, fall back to one request per category in list_incidents_in.
acceptance_criteria: Either verified working (note in issue) or client changed and tests updated.

title: Decision: never create incident.io incidents directly
description: signalman writes alert tags and alert→incident attachments, or feeds an HTTP alert source. incident.io alert routes own incident creation and escalation. Reasons: keeps one routing model, respects the 10 incidents/hour API limit, keeps a human-visible override point in incident.io. Revisit only if alert routes prove unable to express a decision we need.

title: Rename project to signalman
description: Renamed crate, binary, CLI, SIGNALMAN_ADDR, docs, harness and the beads prefix from rustsafe to signalman (PR #4). Remaining owner action: rename the GitHub repository to chussenot/signalman.

title: Documentation set, mise tasks, prek hooks and Claude Code harness
description: README rewritten around the why; docs/ with frontmatter (architecture, client, triage, incident.io, configuration, operations, development, roadmap, three ADRs); mise.toml tools and tasks; prek pre-commit config chained before the beads hooks via scripts/setup-hooks.sh; Claude Code agents (contract-reviewer, question-designer, docs-writer), Bash guard and rustfmt hooks, permission allowlist.
close_reason: Delivered in the tooling commit on claude/rust-typesafe-api-zf13d9

title: Document alert route setup for ai-* tags (with Terraform example)
description: Write docs/incidentio-routing.md: how to filter alert routes on ai-action-page / ai-team-* tags, escalate per team, and suppress ai-action-suppress. Include an incident-io Terraform provider snippet if the provider covers alert routes v3.

title: Act on public_incident.incident_created_v2: suggest severity as a timeline note
description: On incident creation, fetch the incident, ask a Score over the org's severity rubric plus a Noul for customer-facing impact, and POST /v2/incident_timeline_items with the suggestion and confidence for the lead to confirm. Never set severity automatically.
acceptance_criteria: Note appears on a test incident; wording reviewed by an on-call lead.

title: Broaden incident.io coverage
description: Events and endpoints parsed or reachable but not yet acted on.

title: Filter dedup candidates by team and recency before offering them
description: Currently the first 40 open incidents are offered. Prefer incidents updated in the last 24h and, when the alert has a team attribute, those owned by matching team_ids. Reduces tokens and improves candidate coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Candidate selection unit-tested; token usage per triage recorded before and after.

title: Tune Policy thresholds from the evaluation report
description: Using the harness output, pick suppress_below, auto_route_confidence, human_below_confidence, attach_confidence per the docs' three-band approach. Pin the jev version tuned against in Policy docs.
acceptance_criteria: Policy::default updated with rationale in the doc comment; eval report attached.

title: Enrich state with recent changes from deploy sources
description: recent_changes is empty for webhook-triggered triage, so caused_by_change is never asked. Pull deployments for the alert's service from the last 2h (GitHub Deployments API or ArgoCD) and include them in the state.
acceptance_criteria: caused_by_change asked when a deploy exists; ai-suspected-change tag observed on a real regression.

title: Dockerfile and CI image build
description: Multi-stage build (rust:1.94 → distroless or debian-slim), non-root user, HEALTHCHECK on /healthz. Add a CI job that builds the image on PRs and publishes on tags.

title: Readiness endpoint checking upstream reachability
description: /healthz is liveness only. Add /readyz that checks incident.io identity and TypeSafe models list with a short timeout and caches the result for 30s.
acceptance_criteria: Returns 503 with a JSON body naming the failing upstream.

title: Handle private alerts in the webhook flow
description: private_alert.alert_created_v1 carries only the id. With an API key that has private access, fetch and triage like public alerts; otherwise log and skip. Currently ignored silently.

title: Forward alert resolved events with --forward-to-incidentio
description: CLI forwarding only sends status=firing. Accept a status field in the alert JSON and send resolved with the same deduplication_key so the incident.io alert auto-resolves.

value: Architecture rule (decision signalman-p2w, docs/decisions/0001): incident.io stays the alert hub. signalman only writes alert tags (ai-team-*, ai-impact-*, ai-action-*, ai-dup-*, ai-suspected-change) and POST /v2/incident_alerts attachments, or feeds an HTTP alert source with judgments under metadata.ai. Never create incidents directly; alert routes own that.

GitHub Actions on this repository never ran: every job is refused at scheduling with the billing annotation ('recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased'). Check-run annotations are readable unauthenticated at api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/check-runs/<id>/annotations. Nothing in the repo fixes this; the account owner must fix Billing & plans, then re-run. Tracked as signalman-oqj.

incident.io contract: OpenAPI v3 at https://api.incident.io/v1/openapiV3.json (the /v1/openapi.json endpoint is removed, returns 410); guides at https://docs.incident.io/llms.txt; webhooks guide at https://docs.incident.io/api-reference/webhooks.md. Webhooks are Svix-signed (webhook-id/-timestamp/-signature, HMAC-SHA256 over id.ts.body, secret is base64 after whsec_). src/incidentio/webhook.rs is pinned to Svix's published test vector.

Nothing has been run against a real TypeSafe or incident.io account yet (no keys in the dev container). Epic signalman-b11 tracks live verification; the multi-value status_category[one_of] repeated-key filter (signalman-b11.3) is the most likely drift point.

Project renamed from rustsafe to signalman on 2026-09-20 (crate, binary, CLI, env var SIGNALMAN_ADDR, docs, beads prefix). The GitHub repository must be renamed by the owner to chussenot/signalman; git redirects keep the old URL working.

Quality gates before any push: cargo fmt --all --check; RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings cargo clippy --all-targets (pedantic, unwrap_used); cargo test (no network: wiremock mocks both APIs); RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --no-deps. Product names allowed in docs via clippy.toml doc-valid-idents.

TypeSafe docs are the API contract: start at https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt; API reference at /api.md; append .md to any page path for markdown. No Rust SDK exists; src/client.rs mirrors the Python SDK defaults (jev-latest, 10s timeout, 2 retries 0.5s→5s, retry on 408/429/5xx, honour Retry-After).
